items.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime itself that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php; PHP 8.1 and older get no upstream release. Attack traffic is reported and public proofs of concept circulate: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 reports a confirmed intrusion of a European government entity with agentic post-exploitation, from its own telemetry and without naming the victim or the flaw that gave the foothold, while CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation, and VulnCheck holds a working exploit for PHP 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 to 8.5.11 on mod_php. PHP also published an informational advisory for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix: keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular release. BACS knows of no attack in Switzerland but says PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; Swiss cantons, universities, the host Cyon with more than 100,000 sites, the Lodur fire-brigade platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.

items.headline: Two JFrog Artifactory bugs patched weeks ago are confirmed chained into full admin takeover

immediate_action.action: Wiz Research confirms active, ongoing exploitation of this two-CVE chain against self-hosted JFrog Artifactory since 15 August 2026, reaching full administrative control and, in multiple cases, a dropped Rust-based backdoor with C2 capability. Six weeks after disclosure, most organizations running Artifactory still have at least one vulnerable instance. Upgrade every instance to 7.133.11 or later, JFrog's only fixed build for CVE-2026-42016, on a build that also carries the CVE-2026-42018 fix for its branch. Wiz lists 7.133.29, 7.146.38 and 7.161.20 for those branches, above JFrog's own table. Wiz's lower-branch builds 7.111.21, 7.117.28 and 7.125.20 stay inside JFrog's affected range for CVE-2026-42016. Then search access logs for the chain's own signature: an unauthenticated POST to /access/api/v1/aws/token/ followed by a POST to /access/api/v1/tokens from the same client (in some cases Wiz saw an admin account created within five minutes of the first request). A hit where both requests returned HTTP 200 is a successful exploitation: treat the instance as compromised. Revoke all tokens, reset the Access token signing key and certificate, audit for administrator accounts you did not create, remove unauthorized Groovy plugins and restart the JVM to clear any in-memory implant.
immediate_action.title: Patch and hunt JFrog Artifactory now: confirmed admin-takeover chain, backdoors already dropped

items.summary: Citrix's CTX697096 bulletin (2026-09-27) fixes eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, two of which, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, every default deployment) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow to RCE/DoS, reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the VPN-vServer default), were exploited before any fix existed; CISA added both to KEV and Citrix lists no workaround. Mandiant, GTIG, Unit 42, Zscaler and Rapid7 describe the compromises: web-server-configuration persistence, web shells, and in one intrusion the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779 chained with CVE-2026-88771 so that the crash handler ran the payload as root, followed by exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material. An appliance patched after the bulletin therefore still needs a compromise check and its configuration secrets rotated. SAML-configured appliances need the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779 (14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28) and identity providers 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 for CVE-2026-107406; CVE-2026-88773 has a public proof of concept with no exploitation seen.

actions: Apply the BT26-05-RS patch to every self-hosted BeyondTrust Remote Support appliance now and confirm in the /appliance interface that it is installed (a build older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first, which closes the hole but does not undo earlier exposure); apply it to self-hosted Privileged Remote Access appliances too, which BeyondTrust patched as a precaution.

For every appliance that was internet-reachable on a build up to 26.2.3 at any time since late August 2026: before any change, snapshot a virtual appliance with memory and export its disk, and collect the off-box syslog, reverse-proxy or WAF and perimeter firewall logs because the actor deletes on-appliance logs; then redeploy from a clean, fully patched image every appliance whose compromise status is confirmed or unknown, and rotate the credentials it held in dependency order, including the Remote Support Vault and any credential typed into a support session.

items.headline: BeyondTrust patches an exploited Remote Support zero-day; the actor's persistence survives reboot and reset

Apply the BT26-05-RS patch to every self-hosted appliance (builds older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first). The actor's persistence survives reboot and configuration reset and it deletes on-appliance logs, so snapshot and collect off-box logs from any appliance that was internet-reachable on an affected build, then redeploy from a clean patched image any whose compromise status is confirmed or unknown and rotate everything it held.
immediate_action.title: Patch BeyondTrust Remote Support now, review every appliance exposed since late August and rebuild any with confirmed or unknown compromise status

items.headline: Fixed on 20 July, identified on 13 August, probed from 28 July: a CVE-keyed patch process never saw this one coming
items.summary: Zimbra shipped ZCS 10.1.20 on 2026-07-20 with a fix for a command injection in the SNMP monitoring component, and the identifier CVE-2026-73570 followed on 2026-08-13. Microsoft Threat Intelligence now reports confirmed intrusions in more than one region and industry, with probing of the injection point from 2026-07-28, before disclosure, and CISA lists the flaw in KEV (added 2026-08-21). The flaw needs no authentication and applies only where the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled; Microsoft's cases combined web shells, root escalation, theft of Zimbra's authentication keys and cluster-wide movement, so an upgrade does not evict an attacker already inside. actions: On every WordPress site your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with UpdraftPlus, free or premium, including old municipal, campaign and project sites, check for an UpdraftCentral key (wp option get updraft_central_localkeys, or Settings > UpdraftPlus Backups > Advanced Tools > UpdraftCentral) and delete every key even if nobody remembers using UpdraftCentral, then update to 1.26.13 or 2.26.13 or later; deleting a key stops remote management only, and backups keep working.

items.headline: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them
items.summary: TeamUpdraft, the vendor of the UpdraftPlus backup plugin, says unauthorised access to teamupdraft.com on 17 and 18 October probably exposed its customer database, including UpdraftCentral connection keys, and Patchstack and Nethemba report an attacker using those keys to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites, which Patchstack's telemetry dates from 2026-10-18 15:32 (it gives no time zone), and that create hidden administrators. It is not a flaw in UpdraftPlus: the plugin obeys commands signed with a valid key, a key exists on many sites that never used the service because connecting a teamupdraft.com account ticks the option by default, and the update disconnects only connections made before 13:07 BST (12:07 UTC) on 18 October, so keys created later that day have to be deleted by hand. TeamUpdraft says the attacker used a compromised key to enter its own site, and Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21, after 1.26.13 shipped.

actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which now says it must be assumed personal data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.
items.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
items.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Confederation headlined its 2026-10-08 release "data outflow confirmed", and the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Tamedia reports that PK Softech had confirmed in writing in January 2026 that it deleted Publica's 2019 migration data, which apparently stayed on its servers, and that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom; Inside IT relays this and adds that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira took data, and Netzwoche relays that the authorities assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left. Publica says personal data of insured persons has presumably left; the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich says its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Pensionskasse Post says personal data left, the Bernische Pensionskasse says it must be assumed so, the Ticino fund IPCT says data of about 1,800 of its insured persons sat on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more, and other funds are still checking. As of 2026-10-22 neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor or the demand.

In the same tenants review every enterprise application and app registration, MSP management and security tools first but none skipped (Huntress saw the secrets planted on apparently random applications, in one tenant on some of the least privileged ones), for client secrets, certificates and federated credentials added since 2026-10-13 and remove any you did not create; also check the directory roles, owners and consent grants held by ConnectWise and SkyKick service principals, Conditional Access exclusions for them, and mailbox forwarding, inbox and transport rules and delegated access, because disabling the vendor applications does not remove access planted through them.
items.headline: ConnectWise SkyKick app credential used in 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants; disabling it does not undo planted access
items.summary: ConnectWise says it identified unauthorized access to application identities of its Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) service; Huntress and Todyl report that from 15 October the app's credential was used to obtain app-only Microsoft Graph tokens in customer Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress alone confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 tenants by 16 October and saw ConnectWise Cloud Management apps assign themselves directory roles in about 50 tenants and, in two tenants, a scripted Global Administrator self-grant followed by new client secrets planted on apparently random applications. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended the service on 17 October, but says disabling does not reverse changes already made in a tenant, so every tenant that ever consented a ConnectWise or SkyKick app needs the apps disabled and its application credentials, directory roles and consents reviewed. Microsoft assesses that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 is behind it, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework, and says it attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants; how the credential was obtained and what data was read are not public.

actions: Audit every npm publish token your organisation and its maintainers hold and revoke any that can publish without two-factor authentication: that exact token property, not package popularity, is what decides whether the worm spreads from a compromised developer to your packages.

On any developer workstation or build agent that installed a package from the keyv family since 2026-08-04, or tensorlake@0.5.144 since 2026-10-08, treat the AI-assistant, cloud, GitHub, Vault, SSH and Kubernetes credentials present on that host as disclosed and rotate them; the collector sweeps over 300 credential patterns in one pass, so partial rotation leaves the operator a working set. Isolate the host before revoking its GitHub token, because OX Security reports a switch that wipes the machine when the token is revoked; on a host that ran tensorlake@0.5.144, Socket and OX Security also name a token-monitor persistence (a systemd user unit on Linux, a LaunchAgent on macOS, a scheduled task on Windows), which has to be removed before the token is revoked.

Stop treating a valid npm provenance attestation as evidence a package is clean; where release pipelines gate on provenance, change the check to pin on the workflow identity inside the Fulcio certificate and the Rekor log index, which is what Unit 42 says still discriminates.
items.headline: A self-propagating npm worm reaches packages totalling 1.3 billion monthly downloads, and its C2 address lives on-chain
items.summary: Elastic Security Labs identified CHAINDROP on 2026-08-04, a new wave of the Shai-Hulud npm worm that began with the compromise of the keyv maintainer and has backdoored over 400 npm packages whose combined reach Elastic puts at more than 1.3 billion monthly downloads, keyv alone at over 600 million. Execution comes from a package.json preinstall hook that downloads the Bun runtime to run an obfuscated 711 KB payload, which harvests over 300 credential patterns (AI-assistant tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Alibaba credentials, GitHub tokens, Vault tokens, SSH keys and Kubernetes service-account tokens) and self-propagates only when it finds an npm token that both carries package-write permission and can publish without two-factor authentication. Rather than hardcoding a command-and-control domain, CHAINDROP queries an Ethereum smart contract at runtime to resolve where to send the stolen material, so the operator rotates infrastructure without shipping a new payload. On 2026-10-08 a release of the tensorlake npm SDK carried the same payload family with valid build provenance, and Socket and OX Security describe a dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked before its persistence is removed.

actions: Upgrade every Gitea Docker instance that runs with ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION = true to 1.26.4, or until then set REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES to the authenticating proxy's exact address, internet-reachable instances first.

cves.affected: Gitea official Docker image 1.26.2 and earlier, with ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION = true

items.headline: Gitea Docker instances with reverse-proxy login enabled accepted a spoofed login header from anyone, and NCSC-CH rates it exploited
items.summary: Gitea's official Docker image hard-coded REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES to the trust-all wildcard, so on instances where an administrator enabled reverse-proxy authentication, anyone who can reach the container's HTTP port can send an X-WEBAUTH-USER header and be signed in as any user whose login name is known or guessable, admins included (CVE-2026-20896, CVSS 9.8). NCSC-CH set it to actively exploited on 2026-07-10. Sysdig, whose telemetry the public reporting rests on, says the attempt it saw had not progressed to exploitation, though SecurityWeek reports the same telemetry as exploitation. Fixed in 1.26.3, and Gitea recommends 1.26.4.

actions: Patch every PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway to the fixed build in Palo Alto's advisory for its minor release (users then re-authenticate once, because the fixed firewall regenerates the override cookie), or until then disable Authentication Override or give the cookies a certificate that no other feature uses.

On every GlobalProtect gateway that was internet-reachable and unpatched at any time since 2026-05-17, treat the network behind it as a ransomware compromise-assessment target: review VPN sessions that authenticated by cookie from unexpected sources, check Windows hosts for the artifacts Arctic Wolf describes (a ransomware payload staged under C:\\PerfLogs, a PsExec service, an LSASS dump written through comsvcs.dll to an .odt file, an ntdsutil media copy of the Active Directory database, and cleared event logs), and extend the assessment to the virtualization and backup tier: vCenter and ESXi audit logs for a changed execInstalledOnly setting and for access to a domain controller's virtual disk, and the Veeam backup server, because Unit 42 describes one intrusion that pivoted from the gateway to vCenter and dumped domain credentials offline, which in-guest EDR does not see.

cves.affected: PAN-OS 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 below the fixed builds, with a GlobalProtect portal or gateway where authentication override cookies are enabled and a specific certificate configuration exists; Prisma Access 11.2 and 10.2 below the fixed builds

items.headline: Qilin and Inc ransomware exploit the GlobalProtect bypass; one intrusion pivoted to vCenter and ESXi past in-guest EDR
items.summary: CVE-2026-0257 is a pre-auth VPN authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CISA KEV; Palo Alto reports limited exploit attempts, and Rapid7 and Unit 42 report successful exploitation): an attacker forges valid auth-override cookies by re-using the GlobalProtect certificate shared with the HTTPS service, with no credentials. CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) marks it as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with this bypass. Unit 42 now names Qilin and Inc as exploiting it and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi and stole domain credentials offline from a domain controller's virtual disk, which in-guest EDR does not see. Patch or disable auth-override cookies, and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched as a compromise-assessment target that includes the virtualization and backup tier.

actions: Push the 2026-09-05 Pixel security patch level to every managed Pixel device today, prioritising devices issued to personnel who could plausibly be individually targeted by surveillance-grade exploitation (police, government officials, diplomatic staff).

cves.affected: Pixel devices at security patch levels before 2026-09-05

items.headline: Google patches a Pixel modem flaw it says may be under limited, targeted exploitation, and CISA lists it as exploited
items.summary: Google's September 2026 Pixel Update Bulletin (patch level 2026-09-05) fixes CVE-2026-58704, a logic error in the cellular modem that lets a proximal or adjacent attacker bypass permission checks and escalate out of the modem sandbox into the wider device with no user interaction. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-09-16, and Google's bulletin states there are indications it may be under limited, targeted exploitation. Any Pixel device issued to staff who could plausibly be individually targeted needs the update now.

actions: Confirm every Kemp LoadMaster runs GA 7.2.63.2 or LTSF 7.2.54.18 or later, and disable the LoadMaster API wherever it is not required, which removes the /accessv2 attack surface.

For any LoadMaster that was internet-reachable with the API enabled before it was patched, run a compromise assessment of the appliance rather than closing the ticket on the version string: a public exploit has circulated since 2026-06-29.

cves.affected: LoadMaster GA 7.2.60.0 to 7.2.63.1 and LTSF 7.2.54.12 to 7.2.54.17, when the API is enabled; ECS Connections Manager, Object Scale Connection Manager and MOVEit WAF 7.2.60.0 to 7.2.63.1

items.headline: Progress Kemp LoadMaster pre-auth RCE in the /accessv2 API is exploited in the wild and KEV-listed, with fixes in GA 7.2.63.2 and LTSF 7.2.54.18
items.summary: Progress Kemp LoadMaster pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-8037, CVSS 9.6 per Progress, 9.8 per ZDI): uninitialized-malloc heap corruption in the /accessv2 API reaches code execution as root. watchTowr published the full mechanics, exploitation attempts began on 2026-06-29 and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-07; the fix is in GA v7.2.63.2 and LTSF v7.2.54.18.

actions: Upgrade TeamCity On-Premises to 2025.11.7 or 2026.1.3 on the matching branch, or install JetBrains' security-patch plugin where the version is older than that but at least 2017.1, and until that is done restrict external access to the TeamCity server, as JetBrains advises, because the flaw needs nothing but HTTP(S) reachability.

Treat any TeamCity On-Premises server that was internet-reachable and still unpatched at any point after 2026-07-27 as a compromise-assessment target rather than a completed patch: review build-agent registrations for agents you did not enrol, and rotate the VCS credentials, artifact-repository tokens and signing keys the server holds, because an upgrade evicts the entry point but not what was taken through it.

cves.affected: All TeamCity On-Premises versions prior to the branch fixes; TeamCity Cloud already mitigated by JetBrains.
cves.fixed: 2025.11.7 and 2026.1.3, with JetBrains' security-patch plugin as the mitigation path for installations from 2017.1 onward that cannot take the full upgrade.

items.headline: JetBrains patches an unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw reachable on every TeamCity On-Premises version ever shipped
items.summary: JetBrains disclosed CVE-2026-63077 on 2026-07-27: an attacker with nothing more than HTTP(S) access to a TeamCity On-Premises server can exploit the agent-polling protocol to bypass authentication checks and execute arbitrary operating-system commands as the TeamCity server process. Every On-Premises version is affected; fixes are 2025.11.7 and 2026.1.3, with a security-patch plugin available down to 2017.1 for estates that cannot upgrade immediately, and JetBrains says TeamCity Cloud needs no customer action because it is already mitigated. CISA listed the flaw as exploited on 2026-08-05, JetBrains reported active and attempted exploitation of unpatched servers on 2026-08-07, CISA's KEV catalog now marks known ransomware campaign use, and JetBrains' own Cadence service was breached through it. A build server compromise is a supply-chain compromise.

actions: Audit every internet-facing FortiGate for administrator accounts and REST API keys nobody created, then terminate all administrator and VPN sessions and reset every administrator and VPN password.
items.headline: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed is still active, locks admins out of FortiGates and feeds ransomware affiliates
items.summary: FortiBleed is an active credential-compromise campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with SOCRadar counting more than 86,644 compromised devices in 194 countries; Fortinet said in June that it uses no new vulnerability, only reused credentials and brute force. A joint FBI and U.S. Secret Service advisory of 2026-10-06 says attackers keep scanning exposed devices with previously obtained credentials, create administrator accounts on compromised firewalls and in some cases delete or change the original accounts so owners are locked out, and that access brokers using the chain have supplied INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates. An organisation with an internet-exposed FortiGate should end all administrator and VPN sessions, reset every credential and look for accounts and API keys it did not create.

actions: **Patch the LiteSpeed cPanel plugin (CVE-2026-54420)** by upgrading to LiteSpeed WHM PlugIn version 5.3.2.1, which bundles cPanel plugin 2.4.8, or uninstall the user-end plugin until then. It is actively exploited on shared CloudLinux/CageFS hosting. Prioritise any public-sector tenant on shared hosting.

cves.affected: LiteSpeed user-end cPanel plugin before 2.4.8

items.headline: CVE-2026-54420: LiteSpeed cPanel plugin root escalation on CloudLinux/CageFS shared hosting, exploited in the wild (CISA KEV)
items.summary: LiteSpeed user-end cPanel plugin CVE-2026-54420 lets a user with FTP or web-shell access escalate to root on CloudLinux/CageFS shared hosting and is actively exploited; its CVE record dates the in-the-wild exploitation to May 2026, and LiteSpeed was alerted on 2026-05-31 (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01). Added to CISA KEV on 2026-06-15 (CISA, 2026-06-15). Patch to WHM PlugIn 5.3.2.1 (cPanel plugin 2.4.8).

actions: Take every self-hosted Langflow instance off any internet-reachable interface: ZDI documents no fixed version and names restricting interaction with the product as the only mitigation, so network position is the whole of the available control.

On any Langflow host that was internet-exposed, rotate the LLM-provider API keys and any other service credentials that instance held or could read: VulnCheck reports credential harvesting as observed post-exploitation behaviour, and those keys are billable and usable from anywhere.

cves.affected: 1.3.2, the only version ZDI's CVE record lists; no affected range is defined and ZDI's advisory names none
cves.fixed: None documented; ZDI's mitigation is to restrict interaction with the product

items.headline: VulnCheck's canaries show attackers exploiting a Langflow pre-auth RCE with no documented fix and no KEV entry, while the next CVE number is KEV-listed
items.summary: VulnCheck reported on 2026-07-28 that it has observed attackers gaining initial access to Langflow with exploits targeting CVE-2026-0769 and a second Langflow flaw, CVE-2026-5027, then harvesting credentials, deploying cryptominers and attempting lateral movement, without splitting that activity between the two, and that neither flaw is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. CVE-2026-0769 is a Zero Day Initiative 0-day advisory: an eval injection in Langflow's eval_custom_component_code function reachable with no authentication (CVSS 9.8), for which ZDI documents no fixed version and names restricting interaction with the product as the only mitigation. A KEV-driven patch process will not surface this, and the KEV-listed CVE-2026-0770, the next CVE number, is a different vulnerability.

actions: Update Ninja Forms to 3.15.4 or later and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce to 8.6.7 or later on every WordPress site, then check each site for an implant the update does not remove, starting with a comparison of the database's administrator list against the Users screen and an inspection of the must-use plugins directory by content.

On any site where an administrator opened a Ninja Forms submission or a WooCommerce order since 2026-10-04 and an implant turns up, rotate all privileged credentials and the WordPress authentication salts and treat the oldest administrator account as compromised, because a login URL planted by the implant authenticates as that account.

cves.affected: Ninja Forms up to and including 3.15.3
WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce up to and including 8.6.6
Ninja Forms up to and including 3.15.3 (the same flaw as CVE-2026-94504, published by another CVE Numbering Authority)

items.headline: Exploited WordPress plugin XSS ends in a hidden admin and persistence that patching does not remove
items.summary: Patchstack reports that since 2026-10-04 one campaign has been exploiting two unrelated stored cross-site scripting flaws, CVE-2026-93836 in WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce up to 8.6.6 and CVE-2026-94504 in Ninja Forms up to 3.15.3, by planting a script in an order or a form submission that runs when a logged-in administrator opens it. The script uses the administrator's own session to install a malicious plugin and create administrators, one of them hidden from the Users screen, and leaves four independent ways back in, so updating to Ninja Forms 3.15.4 or WPC Product Bundles 8.6.7 stops new injections but does not evict an implant. Patchstack says exploitation volume is limited so far and that the second stage works with any stored XSS that reaches an administrator.

actions: Apply the fixed release for your family listed in ServiceNow security bulletin KB3137947 (Zurich Patch 7b or 9, Yokohama Patch 12 Hot Fix 1b or Patch 13, Australia Patch 2, Brazil EA or GA) to every self-hosted ServiceNow AI Platform instance now; ServiceNow provided these updates to self-hosted customers and partners. Exploitation attempts have been reported since 2026-07-17, and self-hosted instances are the ones ServiceNow did not update itself.

cves.affected: AI Platform instances below the fixed releases listed in KB3137947
cves.fixed: Zurich Patch 7b/9, Yokohama Patch 12 Hot Fix 1b/13, Australia Patch 2, Brazil EA/GA (KB3137947); hosted instances addressed from April

items.headline: ServiceNow AI Platform sandbox escape gives unauthenticated code execution; self-hosted instances need the fixed release
items.summary: ServiceNow disclosed CVE-2026-6875 (CVSS 9.5), a sandbox escape in the ServiceNow AI Platform that, in certain circumstances, lets an unauthenticated user execute code within the platform. ServiceNow addressed its hosted instances starting in April and released updates for self-hosted instances on 2026-07-13. Defused reports exploitation attempts in the wild from 2026-07-17, and NCSC-CH flagged the CVE as actively exploited on 2026-07-20, citing that reporting. ServiceNow's advisory says it is not aware of exploitation against ServiceNow instances, and its spokesperson says it has seen no evidence that the activity relates to instances it hosts. Self-hosted customers and partners must apply the fixed release for their family now, and ServiceNow also encourages hosted customers to apply the patches if they have not already done so.

actions: Upgrade every SAML-configured NetScaler (`add authentication samlAction` or `add authentication samlIdPProfile`) that is still below 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28, 14.1-73.41 FIPS or 13.1-37.282, including appliances on the 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 builds, to at least those builds; identity providers then need the builds named for CVE-2026-107406. Where the upgrade has to wait and NetScaler Console virtual patching is available, confirm with `show appfw signatures` that the Global Deny List signature version is at least v24, which Citrix offers as a bridge for CVE-2026-88779 only.

Before restarting a SAML-configured NetScaler that has crashed or rebooted repeatedly, preserve its logs and crash artifacts, open a Citrix support case, which Citrix asks for when an appliance is experiencing the impact, and search its authentication logs for shell metacharacters next to Pitboss crash-message text, because Rapid7 saw a crash-and-reboot cycle used to make the call-home crash handler run an attacker's payload as root.

cves.affected: NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-73.41; 13.1 before 13.1-64.28; ADC 14.1-FIPS before 14.1-73.41 FIPS; ADC 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP before 13.1-37.282; only when configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider

items.headline: Citrix confirms attacks on a new NetScaler SAML flaw that the September fixed builds do not close
items.summary: Citrix's bulletin CTX697174 fixes CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that a network attacker needing no privileges reaches when the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider; Citrix says it has observed targeted attacks and scopes the impact to denial of service. Appliances already on the 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 builds that fixed the September zero-days remain affected and must move to 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28 or the FIPS builds, and identity-provider appliances then need 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29 or the FIPS builds, which close the further SAML flaw CVE-2026-107406 that Citrix disclosed on 2026-10-08. Reports of code execution on patched honeypots are unconfirmed, and CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 2026-10-04. Rapid7's incident analysis of 2026-10-19 shows the crash used as the reboot trigger of a root-execution chain with CVE-2026-88771 on an affected 14.1 appliance, so repeated crashes on an appliance not yet patched for that flaw call for a compromise check.

actions: Verify the installed build number on every Exchange server directly against the August 2026 fixed builds (KB5121573/74/75/76); do not rely on patch-cycle records showing the update was scheduled or pushed; German BSI telemetry shows most comparable on-prem Exchange operators have not actually applied it two weeks after release.

cves.fixed: Exchange SE RTM 15.2.2562.46 (KB5121573); Exchange 2019 CU15 15.2.1748.49 (KB5121574); Exchange 2019 CU14 15.2.1544.44 (KB5121575); Exchange 2016 CU23 15.1.2507.72 (KB5121576); no Emergency Mitigation workaround exists

items.headline: A working public exploit for an Exchange mailbox-move endpoint lands sixteen days after Patch Tuesday, and MSRC's exploitability rating has not moved
items.summary: CVE-2026-62911 (CVSS3.1 8.0), patched in Microsoft's 11 August 2026 Exchange Server security release and originally rated "Exploitation Less Likely," now has working exploit code published on GitHub (around 27 August 2026). The flaw is a missing channel-binding check on the MRSProxy mailbox-move endpoint that lets a relayed Negotiate authentication exchange be treated as the relayed account, giving an attacker who can relay that exchange full mailbox access across the organization. No in-the-wild exploitation is reported.

For any SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence instance patched with Security Note 3765948 (CVE-2026-44772), configure and maintain the new 'Secure Transformer' system property with an explicit allowed-hosts list for XSL files: the patch alone does not remove the vulnerable servlet, and Onapsis requires the property after the patch so that only XSL files from the listed hosts can be consumed.

cves.fixed: Fixed Commerce Cloud release levels per SAP Security Note 3771065; takes effect only after a rebuild and redeploy

cves.affected: SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence XMII 15.4, 15.5 (SAP Security Note 3758900)
cves.fixed: Per SAP Security Note 3758900; the patch removes the vulnerable servlet component

SAP Commerce Cloud COM_CLOUD 2211, 2211-JDK21 and DHUB_CLOUD 2211, 2211-JDK21 in public-cloud deployments with NGINX (SAP Security Note 3773203)

items.headline: SAP's August patch day is led by a CVSS 10.0 pre-auth code-execution flaw in the Commerce Cloud Data Hub Adapter, fixed only by a rebuild and redeploy
items.summary: SAP's 2026-08-11 Security Patch Day fixes CVE-2026-58231, an improper-authorization flaw in the SAP Commerce Cloud Data Hub Adapter that Onapsis describes as insufficient authorization checks and input validation and SAP describes as reachable without authentication, rated CVSS 10.0 and capable of arbitrary code execution. Further notes cover code injection in SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence (CVE-2026-44772, 9.9; CVE-2026-44758, 9.1) and an unauthenticated memory-corruption flaw in the NetWeaver AS ABAP kernel's DIAG protocol parser (CVE-2026-34265, 9.8). Defused later reported exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-58231 at its honeypots; Commerce Cloud fixes require rebuilding and redeploying the release rather than installing a patch, and an IP filter set is the vendor-side interim control.

actions: Upgrade every self-hosted Metabase to at least 0.58.24 / 0.59.21 / 0.60.17 / 0.61.11 / 0.62.9 / 0.63.5, then, for any instance that was reachable and unpatched during the exploitation window, revoke all active sessions by clearing the core_session table, delete unrecognised API keys, and rotate the credentials for every connected database and warehouse, not just the Metabase admin credentials, because the upgrade does not invalidate what was already retrieved.

Search Metabase application or reverse-proxy ingress logs across the entire pre-upgrade exposure window for a POST to /api/session/reset_password returning HTTP 400 immediately followed by a GET to /api/user/current returning HTTP 200 from the same source; Metabase states that sequence indicates the instance was likely compromised.

cves.affected: Metabase Cloud and self-hosted releases in the 58 through 63 branches
cves.fixed: latest patched release for each affected self-hosted branch; Metabase Cloud patched by the vendor

items.headline: Metabase Cloud was breached through its own 0-day; self-hosted instances stay vulnerable until manually upgraded
items.summary: Metabase disclosed on 2026-08-06 that its Metabase Cloud platform was attacked through a previously unknown vulnerability in versions 1.58 and above: an unauthenticated attacker injects arbitrary SQL against the application database and obtains administrator access to the instance, from which they can rewrite configuration, steal the stored credentials for every connected database and export the data those connections reach. The only interim workaround the vendor offers is to block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint, which is also where its published attack pattern runs. Cloud instances were patched by the vendor; self-hosted deployments stay vulnerable until manually upgraded to 0.58.24, 0.59.21, 0.60.17, 0.61.11, 0.62.9 or 0.63.5. Laptop maker Framework and form builder Tally were the first to confirm customer data was taken, on 2026-08-03. The flaw went a week without a CVE identifier before it was assigned CVE-2026-72898 and added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-11. VenariX now tracks fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents and ties two of them, at Statista and Dodo Payments, to the Dire Wolf extortion group working against self-hosted instances.

actions: Find every workflow in your GitHub organisations that references actions-cool/issues-helper or actions-cool/maintain-one-comment by tag; where either ran successfully on 2026-05-18 to 05-19 or 2026-09-16 to 09-25, rotate every secret that workflow could read and check the repository's commits since 2026-09-16 for added Claude Code or VS Code hook files, then remove the action or pin it to a full commit SHA from before 2026-05-18.
items.headline: The compromised actions-cool GitHub Actions were re-enabled in September with malicious tags and ran the payload again
items.summary: On 2026-05-18 all 53 version tags of the actions-cool/issues-helper GitHub Action, and all 15 of actions-cool/maintain-one-comment, were moved to imposter commits whose payload reads the Runner.Worker process memory for decrypted workflow secrets and sends them over HTTPS to an attacker-controlled domain (StepSecurity); Socket places the compromise in the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. GitHub disabled both repositories on 2026-05-19 but they became reachable again on 2026-09-16 with the malicious tags intact, so tag-referencing workflows ran the payload again and SafeDep counted six newly infected repositories by 2026-09-24, until GitHub disabled both again by 2026-09-25 (Socket, The Hacker News). Only workflows pinned to a full commit SHA from before 2026-05-18 were unaffected.

actions: Patch every Unbound resolver at 1.26.0 or older to 1.26.1 now, including resolvers that do not validate DNSSEC: NLnet Labs lists CVE-2026-82717 for every version up to 1.26.0 with no validation precondition.
items.headline: A malicious zone Unbound is only asked to resolve can overflow its DNSSEC validator's digest buffer
items.summary: NLnet Labs' Unbound 1.26.1 security release fixes nine vulnerabilities, among them two heap-corruption flaws affecting every version through 1.26.0 that it rates critical and high: CVE-2026-81642, a DNSSEC-validator digest-buffer overflow triggered by a DNSKEY record whose owner name uses a self-referencing compression pointer, and CVE-2026-82717, a companion CNAME-synthesis heap overflow during upstream response processing. Both can reach remote code execution; NCSC Switzerland records exploitation status as unknown. Every Unbound resolver at 1.26.0 or older must patch to 1.26.1 now: CVE-2026-81642 needs DNSSEC validation, and NLnet Labs names no such precondition for CVE-2026-82717.

actions: Copy the application and network logs of every self-hosted Zammad instance, then upgrade it to Zammad 7.2.2 (7.2.0 is affected by the 27 advisories Zammad published on 2026-10-06); a 6.5 instance that cannot be upgraded yet gets the 6.5.5 emergency fix from Zammad's new 6.5 package repository, and an older instance that cannot be upgraded goes offline.

On every instance that was internet-reachable on 6.3.0 to 6.5.4 since 2026-09-21, run DIVD's log-check script, and treat a hit, or any DEB or RPM host where code ran as the zammad account, as compromised.

cves.affected: Zammad 6.3.0 through 6.5.4 (DIVD's case page and NCSC-NL); the DIVD CVE record states >= 6.3.0 to < 6.5.4; Zammad says exploitation is possible only on 6.5 and older; 7.0.0 through 7.1.3 contain the defect but DIVD says it is not exploitable there because of environment conditions
cves.fixed: Zammad: 7.0 and later are not affected and 7.2.0 hardens the code; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) carries further security fixes and 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) is the current release; 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the unsupported 6.5 series, installed from a new package repository; older branches receive no security fixes; NCSC-NL says an update exists and DIVD recommends upgrading to Zammad 7

cves.affected: DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations of every released packaged version before 7.2.2 (Zammad advisory GHSA-p97w-927q-8vxq; DIVD's CVE record: >= 1.5.0 to < 7.2.2); installations from source and the official container images are not affected; DIVD's case page had said all versions including the latest alpha
cves.fixed: 7.2.2 (2026-10-08, Zammad release notes; DIVD's CVE record lists 7.2.2 and later as unaffected). Zammad's advisory page of 2026-10-05 still says its team is working on a solution, so the vendor's pages disagree on status; NCSC-NL had said on 2026-09-30 that the flaw was not yet fixed

items.headline: Zammad 6.5.5 is an emergency fix for the exploited session-leak RCE on 6.5; 7.2.2 fixes the root escalation
items.summary: DIVD, the Dutch vulnerability-disclosure CSIRT, says attackers entered its network on 2026-09-21 through two Zammad flaws it calls previously unknown: CVE-2026-102489, a session hijack leading to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0 to 6.5.4, and CVE-2026-102490, a local escalation from that user to root. NCSC-NL states both have been exploited since 21 September and CISA listed both in KEV on 2026-10-02; Zammad says the code-execution flaw is exploitable only on 6.5 and older, and Horizon3 published the root cause and a working exploit for it on 2026-10-07. Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations, and 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the code-execution flaw in the otherwise unsupported 6.5 series; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) had fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited.

items.summary: Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 fixes CVE-2026-21589, an unauthenticated arbitrary file access flaw in every version of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, plus Crucible and Fisheye (CVSS 4.0 9.3), and tells customers to patch immediately or take internet-facing instances off the internet. watchTowr Labs published the root cause, the request shape and a runnable checker on 2026-10-06, and exploitation attempts followed the same day: Previdian's honeypot sensors recorded attempts from dozens of addresses in about twenty countries, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts on its own honeypots, and a Nuclei template exists; neither honeypot operator reports a compromise. items.headline: An attacker can reconstruct admin credentials for an exposed refrigeration controller offline, then silently disable cooling while the display reports normal
items.summary: Claroty Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities (21 high) in Copeland XWEB300D/500D/500B PRO supervisory refrigeration controllers. Three chain to unauthenticated root RCE: an auth-bypass logic flaw in the Lua authentication handler, a deterministic admin-password generator derivable offline from the device's MAC address and current date, and an unauthenticated OS command injection via the libraries installation route. 18 further, authenticated-only command-injection flaws score CVSS 8.0 each, and CISA's advisory adds two low-severity unauthenticated flaws. Copeland fixed all 23 in firmware v1.13; no source read reports exploitation of these flaws, but CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-13 now reports numerous compromises of Copeland xweb refrigeration controllers without naming models, flaws or the entry vector.

items.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. items.headline: Fifty credential-free, no-interaction flaws span Oracle's middleware, ERP, BI and telco-assurance lines in an off-quarter patch release
items.summary: Oracle's September 2026 Critical Security Patch Update, published 2026-09-15, carries 673 patches of which 153 are for Fusion Middleware, and Oracle states 78 of those may be exploited over a network without credentials. Oracle's own risk matrix lists fifty CVEs at CVSS 9.8-10.0 that are network-reachable without privileges or user interaction and marked remotely exploitable without authentication. Six are CVSS 10.0 flaws in WebLogic Server, Access Manager, Forms, Internet Directory, Platform Security for Java and Hyperion Financial Management, and forty-four are CVSS 9.8 flaws across Fusion Middleware (Access Manager, Forms, Internet Directory and Platform Security for Java again, plus Data Integrator, Identity Manager, JDeveloper, WebCenter Enterprise Capture/Portal/Sites, WebLogic Server and Service Delivery Platform) and other product lines: E-Business Suite, Hyperion Financial Management, Business Intelligence/BI Publisher, Enterprise Manager, Communications Unified Assurance and Product Lifecycle Analytics. No exploitation is reported for any of the fifty. The release is Oracle's off-quarter patch line, which a calendar built only on the quarterly dates will miss.

items.summary: Novee Security's Black Hat USA 2026 write-up root-causes trust-boundary failures in AI coding-agent CI harnesses, each tested against the vendor's own public repository in default configuration. Against Claude Code Action it reports three successive rounds of patch-and-bypass, of which only the last (an allowlist entry that pre-approved a bare hostname for the fetch tool) carries CVE-2026-54316; the two more instructive rounds, a command validator that strips single-quoted content before inspecting it and a read-only allowlist exempt from path checking, carry no identifier. Google's advisory for the Gemini CLI findings, aliased CVE-2026-12537, hardens headless folder trust and tool allowlisting under yolo mode. items.summary: Patchstack reports that CVE-2026-85097, an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in the Pro Forms module of Bricksforge, a paid WordPress add-on for the Bricks page builder, has been targeted in the wild since 2026-10-07: it lets an attacker with no account get a PHP file written to the uploads directory and executed, on versions up to and including 3.1.8.9 with Pro Forms active (about 6,000 active installations). Bricksforge's revised changelog states the flaw was fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0 and lists a related Pro Forms upload fix in 4.0.1 of 2026-10-08; the exploitation report rests on Patchstack's telemetry.

items.headline: Drupal patches a critical Field UI RCE reachable through contributed modules; uninstall field_ui if you cannot update
items.summary: Drupal's advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-108097, a remote code execution flaw in the core Field UI module rated Critical (19 of 25): core alone is not directly exploitable, but several exploit paths exist through contributed modules and at least one known path needs no login. Fixed releases are 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below and Drupal 8 and 9 get no fix, and until a site is updated the advisory's mitigation is to uninstall the Field UI module. The advisory records no public exploit at publication, and The Hacker News relays the Security Team's pre-announcement warning that exploits might be developed within hours or days.

items.headline: Adobe fixes unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce; no exploitation known
items.summary: Adobe's 2026-10-13 bulletins fix five unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 in ColdFusion 2025 and 2023 (fixed in 2025.0.14 and 2023.0.26), three unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 code-execution flaws in Experience Manager (Cloud Service 2026.9.28386 or per-issue hotfixes) and two code-execution flaws (CVSS 10.0 and 9.8) in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (2026-oct builds). Adobe says it knows of no exploitation of any of them; each needs no account, so exposure rather than exploitation status decides the order. Sansec reproduced four code-execution routes for the Commerce flaw CVE-2026-103849 within 24 hours of the fix, sees no exploitation yet, and warns that a Composer install keeps the vulnerable base version until the 2026-oct release or Adobe's isolated patch is applied.

items.headline: Microsoft ties JADEPUFFER's cloud operations to two Azure service principals: one enumerated a tenant for 15+ hours, the other destroyed resources in minutes
items.summary: Microsoft Security Research documents Azure resource-destruction activity it associates with JADEPUFFER (tracked by Microsoft as Storm-3168), the actor Sysdig disclosed in July 2026 as the first documented agentic-ransomware operation. Of two compromised service principals from one tenant, one enumerated resources for over 15 hours; the second ran a roughly seven-minute destructive burst that attempted 100+ storage-account deletions (most succeeded, some blocked by resource locks), deleted a Key Vault, a Function App and an App Service plan, and attempted to delete Azure Site Recovery and Backup protection locks before harvesting storage-account keys. Timing evidence points to automated, scripted execution. Microsoft says it is unclear how the service principal was compromised. As possible initial access it notes a service-principal secret an employee posted in plaintext in a public GitHub issue, which stayed retrievable through the issue's edit history after redaction, but it could not confirm that secret was used.

items.headline: AI coding agents' plugin SHA-pinning is bypassable, mainly via plugins hosted on Bitbucket or self-hosted git, and only consumer Gemini CLI stays unfixed
items.summary: AIR Security disclosed Plugin4Shell (2026-09-17): a design flaw present in Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI, none of which verified after checkout that a plugin's working tree matches its marketplace-pinned commit hash, so a repository owner can swap malicious code into an installed, trusted plugin on its next update. The branch-name trick needs a git host that accepts hash-shaped branch names, such as Bitbucket or a self-hosted server (GitHub and GitLab reject them), and auto-update is on by default only for the agents' built-in GitHub-hosted marketplaces; Gemini CLI's variant is not clearly blocked on GitHub. OpenAI's own fix shipped in Codex 0.146.0, AIR says Claude Code 2.1.179 is fixed, heise online reports, citing GitHub support, that Copilot CLI 1.0.87 and the Copilot app 1.1.23 carry a fix, and Google is retiring consumer Gemini CLI instead of fixing it.

actions: Audit domain-root and OU-linked GPOs for unexpected Files, Registry or Security Settings client-side-extension entries (ransom-note file drops, legal-notice banner rewrites, local Administrator account disablement, Windows Firewall disablement).
items.headline: Kaspersky GERT: a Group Policy Object was the whole ransomware on Windows, in a channel most EDR tools do not inspect
items.summary: Kaspersky's Global Emergency Response Team reconstructs an April 2026 incident at a Middle East manufacturing organization in which an attacker with GPO-write privileges authored a Group Policy Object that dropped ransom notes, disabled the local Administrator account and replaced the lock-screen wallpaper domain-wide across every Windows workstation, plus a second, independently deployed Group Policy Object that disabled Windows Firewall, using only native Group Policy client-side extensions: no ransomware binary, no file encryption and no endpoint persistence on any Windows system. Separately, Kaspersky found a PAYLOAD ransomware sample targeting ESXi on the organization's Linux servers, and data exfiltrated from file servers was later published on the dark web.

items.headline: Microsoft ships the engine fix for RoguePlanet (CVE-2026-50656), the Defender SYSTEM-level LPE NCSC-CH has tracked with a public PoC since June
items.summary: NCSC-CH's Nightmare Eclipse tracker was updated on 2026-07-09 to record that a CVE has been assigned to RoguePlanet (CVE-2026-50656), a link-following (CWE-59) local privilege escalation in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine behind Defender that lets a local attacker reach SYSTEM; Microsoft's MSRC record shows the engine fix has now shipped. A public PoC existed from 2026-06-09 and the CVE sat without a fix for over three weeks. The engine auto-updates, so most estates are already current, but WSUS-gated, offline or OT-adjacent estates should explicitly verify the installed engine build. NCSC-CH later recorded an alleged bypass of the fix, ShieldBreak (CVE-2026-69414), which Microsoft fixed in engine 1.1.26080.3.

items.headline: MikroTik's long-term changelogs already carry the fix for a pre-auth RouterOS RCE; its notice still says pending
items.summary: MikroTik's notice of 2026-10-06 describes CVE-2026-84411, an integer underflow in HTTP request body handling of the RouterOS web management service (WebFig, on the www and www-ssl ports) that one crafted request sent without logging in can use to crash the service or run code on the router with full privileges; CISA scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8. RouterOS before 7.24, v6 included, is affected where an attacker can reach the web interface; 7.24 fixes the v7 stable channel and MikroTik's changelogs list the fix in 7.23.8 (v7 long-term, 2026-10-08) and 6.49.23 (v6 long-term, 2026-10-07), although its notice still shows both long-term releases as pending; MikroTik says the default firewall already blocks the web interface from the internet, and CISA records no known public exploitation.
